1.text: Here, you have two powerful ways to listen.
With Read mode on the left, you can hear any selected text read aloud word-for-word.
You can choose from dozens of natural voices and adjust reading speeds from 0.75x up to 2x.
On the right is Summary mode, powered by NotebookLM.
It extracts key ideas from lengthy articles, and you can even listen in an engaging two-voice podcast format.
Let's move to Step 2 to explore API keys and Gemini setup.

2.text: Step 2 is connecting your API keys.
AI Productivity Flow includes Microsoft Edge voices completely free out of the box.
To unlock Gemini AI, Deepgram, or OpenAI, click the Gemini card right here.
Click 'Get API Key' to open Google AI Studio in one click, copy your free key, paste it in the field, and tap 'Test Connection' to verify it.
All keys are stored and encrypted locally on your computer.
Next, let's explore history and audio downloads.

3.text: Step 3 is your Audio Summary History.
You can toggle this bar open or closed anytime to see your past work.
Every summary you create is automatically saved in your offline library.
You can search past notes, replay waveforms, and download the MP3 audio file with one click—perfect for listening on your phone during your commute or sharing with your team.
Next, let's see how to use Audio Flow directly on your screen!

4.text: Finally, the true superpower of Audio Flow is that you never need to copy-paste or switch apps.
Whenever you are reading an article on Twitter, browsing in Chrome, or reading a PDF, simply highlight any text.
An instant floating quick-action menu appears right by your cursor.
Click Summary or Read, and a floating player appears on your desktop with live waveforms and playback controls while you keep working.
You're now ready to use Audio Flow.
